dimensions.name: Contract & semantics reverse-engineering

evidence.note: Systematic upfront reading of helpers.py, conftest, run.sh, readme, and the public tests (twice) to extract the concrete request/response shapes the first-party client exercises — the core contract-extraction activity for this dimension.

Checked available packages/network (deliberate library choice), read the oracle fixtures (LibreOffice ground truth), and inspected the xlsx internal structure — grounding the openpyxl round-trip and value-comparison semantics rather than guessing.
Task decomposition explicitly names the spill ghost/kind discriminator/workbooks envelope/collab framing, showing the extracted wire contract was internalized into a working model.

Probed genuinely tricky Excel/LibreOffice semantics as each subsystem was reached — xlsx+CF round-trip, collab backfill, goal-seek/iterative fixed-point, SUMIF/COUNTIF criteria and blanks — i.e. contract/semantics re-consultation sustained through the build, not only at the start.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent front-loads a thorough, multi-source extraction of the wire contract from helpers.py, run.sh, the smoke tests, oracle fixtures, and xlsx internals, and verifies library/package availability — matching the level-8 'systematically maps every payload the client touches, probes Excel semantics for tricky areas, verifies chosen libraries' description. It also re-consults Excel/LibreOffice semantics as new subsystems (xlsx CF, collab, goal-seek, criteria functions) are reached, showing contract-driven work beyond the opening. It falls short of 10 because there is no visible durable cross-referenced contract-map artifact or explicit surfacing/resolution of ambiguities from observed client behavior.

dimensions.name: Sequencing the feature surface into checkable milestones

evidence.note: Eleven TaskCreate calls decompose the huge surface into subsystem milestones ordered by dependency: server/health/persistence/CRUD first, then parser, then functions, then dep-graph/recompute/spill, then patch/fill/sort, then xlsx, analyst surface, collab, iterative+goalseek, SPA. A real dependency-aware sequence, not a flat feature list.

Engine and cycle/iterative-calc (the high-risk recompute/graph layer) are smoke-tested and debugged before the server is even written — partial front-loading of the load-bearing layer's correctness as a done-check.
TaskUpdate in_progress/completed markers throughout show live tracking of milestone state as each subsystem is finished and the dev suite is re-run (132,147,151).

A distinct second wave of verification milestones with concrete behavioral done-checks: perf budgets (1000-chain, 100k import <30s/recompute<10s, 5000 dependents <2s), state survives restart, additional formula corpus + Playwright journey. Done-criteria expressed as verifiable behavior.

Counter-evidence: nearly the entire codebase is written in one burst before the server starts (130) and the suite runs (132), rather than getting a live server + core cell round-trip green before building breadth — the discipline anchor 8 describes.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent produced a genuine dependency-ordered decomposition of the feature surface into subsystem milestones (20-30) plus a dedicated verification-milestone layer with concrete runnable done-checks (160-163), tracked live via TaskUpdate — clearly above anchor 5's 'sensible phases with rough checkpoints.' It falls short of anchor 8/10 because build was largely big-bang (write everything, then test) rather than getting core round-trip green before breadth, per-build-milestone done-checks were mostly the shared dev suite rather than individually specified, and the plan was extended rather than re-ordered as scope deepened. That places it at a 7, interpolating between 5 and 8.

dimensions.name: Self-built verification beyond the smoke suite

evidence.note: Self-built engine tests during build: formula smoke tests, dependency/cycle/spill/aggregate checks, plus instrumented debugging of cycle detection and iterative calc on clear — verification steering fixes.
Ran full dev smoke suite, pulled failure details, applied targeted fixes across evaluator/server/tokenizer/operations, then re-ran to confirm — failure-driven loop, not just a green-run-and-done.
Created explicit verification tasks and ran performance benchmarks against the stated ceilings (1000-cell chain, 100k import), i.e. probing the performance bounds directly.
Persistence-across-restart probe surfaced a deserialize bug that was diagnosed and fixed — verification uncovering a real defect.
XLSX round-trip verified via openpyxl re-import and conditional-format style preservation, driving ~15 iterative xlsx.py edits until fidelity held.
Broad subsystem probes: collab backfill/dependents, goal-seek convergence + no-dependency rejection, iterative toggle, Excel edge cases (SUMIF/COUNTIF fixes), cross-sheet/locale/validation variants.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent built targeted checks well beyond the smoke suite across nearly every subsystem — formula oracles, error-sentinel edge cases, spill, xlsx openpyxl round-trip, collab, goal-seek, iterative calc, locale, persistence — and benchmarked the stated performance ceilings, consistently using failures to drive fixes; this meets and exceeds the breadth of anchor 8. It falls short of 10 because the checks are disposable inline probes rather than a persistent systematic harness, and expected values appear largely hand-asserted rather than systematically grounded in the LibreOffice oracle corpus.

dimensions.name: Tracking done-vs-remaining across a huge surface

evidence.note: Creates ~13 explicit TaskCreate entries upfront mapping the full feature surface (server, parser, function catalog, recompute, xlsx, analyst surface, collab, iterative/goal-seek, SPA), establishing a live ledger of endpoint families.
Sustained TaskUpdate in_progress/completed transitions as subsystems finish (parser, recompute, REST layer), maintaining an accurate running state picture rather than vague mental tracking.
Tasks marked completed only after the full dev suite and persistence checks pass — status reconciled against verification results, not just self-report.
Ledger evolves: after core build, adds new verification tasks (perf budgets, persistence, formula-family/Playwright), showing continued tracking of remaining work.
Debugging sessions (cycle detection, xlsx round-trip, SUMIF/COUNTIF criteria) each converge via instrument→fix→re-verify and end with regression re-runs, not circular looping on the same failure.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent maintains a live, granular ledger at the endpoint-family level via TaskCreate/TaskUpdate, transitions statuses as areas complete, adds verification tasks as the horizon shifts, and marks completion reconciled against test runs — clearly above anchor 5's static checklist and matching most of anchor 8's live-ledger and non-looping-debugging traits. It falls short of 8-10 because tracking granularity is family-level rather than the full ~150-function catalog, and there is no explicit evidence of detecting thrashing and deliberately reallocating effort, placing it at a 7 between the 5 and 8 anchors.

dimensions.name: Course-correcting on falsified Excel/perf assumptions

evidence.note: Cycle-detection and clear-propagation bug: repeated instrument/debug steps ('Trace affected set and cycle detection on clear', 'Instrument recompute on clear') driving edits to workbook.py and re-tests — root-cause investigation of the dependency-graph/recompute model rather than a single local patch.
Ran full dev suite, pulled failure details, made targeted fixes across evaluator/server/tokenizer/operations, then restarted and re-ran the suite — reacting to falsified behavior and re-verifying.

Persistence-across-restart test failed; agent diagnosed the restart/deserialize failure and reworked store.py + workbook.py serialization, then restarted and verified the fix — recognized a wrong assumption in the persistence contract.

XLSX round-trip failure led to reading xlsx.py to understand structure, then reworking it and finishing with a full dev-suite regression check (step 227) — reworked a subsystem and guarded unaffected ones.

Excel edge-case tests surfaced COUNTIF-blank / SUMIF-criteria divergences; agent debugged, fixed funcs_common, re-verified, and re-ran the full suite — grounding fixes in Excel semantics and re-verifying.

dimensions.reasoning: Across multiple subsystems (cycle/clear recompute, persistence deserialize, xlsx round-trip, COUNTIF/SUMIF semantics) the agent repeatedly detected divergence from verification signals, diagnosed the responsible design (often with explicit instrumentation and source reads), reworked it, and re-verified — including regression runs of the full suite to avoid derailing other subsystems. This is squarely the level-8 behavior (reworks the relevant design rather than piling on patches) with some reach toward 9; it falls short of 10 because most verification followed big-bang construction rather than continuous early steering, and I only have the tool-call index (not observations) to confirm diagnosis depth.

dimensions.name: Coverage allocation under finite effort

evidence.note: Created ~11 tasks partitioning the ENTIRE surface (all function families, all endpoint families, xlsx, collab, analyst surface, SPA), establishing a breadth-first allocation across everything graded rather than deep-diving one area.
Implemented all function families and endpoint families in dependency order with no rabbit-holing on any single niche function/feature — broad coverage secured before edge-case work.

Dedicated verification phase concentrated on high-value/high-risk surfaces (perf budgets, persistence, broad formula corpus, xlsx round-trip, collab, goal seek) and edge cases on COMMON functions (SUMIF/COUNTIF), reflecting return-weighted effort allocation.
When edge cases surfaced (COUNTIF blanks, SUMIF criteria), fixed and moved on rather than over-polishing — but this was reactive, without explicit timeboxing/deferral reasoning.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent's observed behavior clearly exceeds anchor 5 (rough prioritization): it deliberately built breadth-first coverage across the whole catalog and endpoint families before deep edge-case verification, and it concentrated its late-stage verification effort on high-value/high-risk areas without rabbit-holing. It falls short of a full 8/10 because the (condensed) trajectory shows no explicit reasoning about what NOT to over-invest in, no conscious deferral or timeboxing of low-yield niches (distributions/engineering were built at equal weight), and no marginal-yield reallocation. That places it at a 7 — between rough prioritization and explicit graded-return reasoning.

rubric.task_read: This is an extremely long-horizon, high-complexity build: a full Excel-clone product (persistent HTTP server + SPA + WebSocket collab) with a formula engine spanning ~150 functions, Excel-365 dynamic arrays/spill, a dependency graph with performance-bounded dirty recompute, xlsx/CSV round-trip, and a large analyst surface (defined names, formats, conditional formatting, pivots, locale, validation, goal seek, iterative calc). The exact wire contract is under-specified and must be reverse-engineered from an existing Python client, and grading is on a much larger HIDDEN suite plus value-by-value comparison against a LibreOffice oracle. This task demands maximal, sustained meta-work across all five faculties: deep upfront orientation on the contract, aggressive decomposition/sequencing of an enormous surface, self-built verification well beyond the smoke suite, tight progress tracking, and constant course-correction as Excel edge cases falsify assumptions.

dimensions.name: Contract & semantics reverse-engineering
dimensions.description: Extracting the exact wire shapes from /dev_tests/helpers.py and the smoke suite, and grounding formula/feature behavior in Excel/LibreOffice semantics, before and while building.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The wire shapes are defined ONLY by what the first-party client calls, and grading compares values against a LibreOffice oracle. Guessing shapes or semantics guarantees hidden-suite failures no matter how good the code is; this is the single highest-leverage meta-activity here.

anchors.0: Starts writing the server/engine without reading helpers.py or dev_tests; invents endpoint and cell shapes from imagination.
anchors.3: Skims helpers.py once; picks up a few obvious shapes but leaves most of the contract (patch/fill/sort/spill/collab payloads, kind discriminator, envelope) inferred loosely.
anchors.5: Reads helpers.py and run.sh to extract the concrete request/response shapes it exercises, chooses libraries (OOXML I/O, formula eval) deliberately, and forms a working model of the core cell/formula contract.
anchors.8: Systematically maps every endpoint, discriminator, and payload the client touches into an explicit reference; probes Excel semantics for genuinely tricky areas (spill ghosts, #SPILL!/#CIRC!, iterative fixed-point, locale canonicalization, xlsx openpyxl round-trip) rather than assuming; verifies chosen libraries actually support required features (CF, styles, named ranges).
anchors.10: Builds a durable, cross-referenced contract map reconciling helpers.py, the smoke suite, and Excel/LibreOffice ground truth; proactively surfaces ambiguities and resolves them from observed client behavior; re-consults the client/oracle as new subsystems are reached, so implementation is contract-driven throughout rather than only at the start.

dimensions.name: Sequencing the feature surface into checkable milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking an enormous, interdependent surface into an ordered hierarchy of sub-goals — each with an explicit done-check — sequenced by dependency and risk.
dimensions.why_it_matters: There are dozens of endpoint families and ~150 functions with hard dependencies (health/persistence → contract → engine → graph → dynamic arrays → analyst surface → collab/xlsx). Without deliberate ordering and done-criteria, the agent cannot sustain progress or know when a layer is solid enough to build on.

anchors.0: Treats the whole product as one undifferentiated push; jumps between unrelated features with no ordering or completion criteria.
anchors.3: A flat, one-time to-do list of features with no dependency ordering and no per-item way to know it's done.
anchors.5: Phases the work into sensible stages (skeleton/health first, then engine, then extras) with rough checkpoints per stage.
anchors.8: An explicit milestone hierarchy sequenced by dependency and risk (get a live server + persistence + contract-correct core cell round-trip green before breadth), each milestone with a concrete done-check tied to a runnable test.
anchors.10: A living, dependency-aware milestone plan that front-loads the highest-risk load-bearing layers (dependency graph, spill, recompute correctness/performance), defines done-criteria in terms of verifiable behavior, and is revisited and re-ordered as scope understanding deepens — never a static checklist.

dimensions.name: Self-built verification beyond the smoke suite
dimensions.description: Deliberately constructing checks — formula-value oracles, round-trip tests, error-sentinel and performance probes — rather than trusting the non-exhaustive smoke suite.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The spec explicitly warns the visible suite is non-exhaustive and grading is a much larger hidden suite plus cell-by-cell comparison to LibreOffice. An agent that only runs run.sh is flying blind on the majority of what's graded.

anchors.0: No verification; assumes code works, or never runs the provided smoke suite.
anchors.3: Runs dev_tests/run.sh occasionally and treats a green smoke run as done.
anchors.5: Runs the smoke suite regularly and hand-checks a few formulas/endpoints against expected Excel values.
anchors.8: Builds its own targeted tests well beyond the smoke suite — spot-checking function outputs against known Excel results, exercising error sentinels, spill collisions, xlsx round-trip via openpyxl, and the stated performance bounds — using failures to drive fixes.
anchors.10: Stands up a systematic verification harness covering breadth of the catalog and subsystems (dynamic arrays, collab seq/broadcast, locale, iterative calc, goal-seek convergence, xlsx fidelity), grounds expected values in an Excel/LibreOffice oracle, benchmarks the performance ceilings, and treats verification as the primary signal steering what to build/fix next.

dimensions.name: Tracking done-vs-remaining across a huge surface
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate live picture of which functions, endpoints, and subsystems are complete vs outstanding, and detecting stuck/circular states.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With ~150 functions and ~15 feature families over a very long horizon, it is easy to lose the plot, double-implement, or silently drop whole categories; sustained accurate tracking is what prevents both gaps and thrash.

anchors.0: No sense of what's done or left; forgets whole feature areas or repeatedly reworks the same thing without noticing.
anchors.3: Vague mental tracking; periodically rediscovers unfinished areas by accident.
anchors.5: Keeps a checklist of major features and updates it as areas are completed.
anchors.8: Maintains a live, granular ledger of the function catalog and endpoint families (done / partial / not-started), and notices when it is stuck or re-debugging the same issue, adjusting rather than looping.
anchors.10: Sustains an accurate running picture across the entire surface for the whole horizon, reconciled against verification results (not just self-report), promptly detects thrashing/circular debugging or a stalled subsystem, and reallocates effort deliberately in response.

dimensions.name: Course-correcting on falsified Excel/perf assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising design or approach when reality — Excel edge cases, spill/recompute behavior, performance limits, contract mismatches — diverges from expectations.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Excel semantics and the dependency/spill/iterative machinery are riddled with edge cases; initial designs (e.g. naive recompute, spill handling, locale parsing) will be falsified. Barrelling ahead on a wrong assumption compounds into wide test failures.

anchors.0: Ignores contradicting evidence; keeps pushing a falsified design (e.g. recompute that misses dependents or blows the perf budget) unchanged.
anchors.3: Reacts only to hard crashes with local patches; doesn't revisit the underlying approach when results are subtly wrong.
anchors.5: Fixes issues as tests surface them and makes reasonable local design changes when something clearly doesn't work.
anchors.8: Recognizes when a failure signals a wrong assumption (dependency-graph model, spill materialization, topological order, contract shape) and reworks the relevant design rather than piling on patches.
anchors.10: Detects divergence early from verification signals, diagnoses the root assumption, revises the affected design deliberately, and re-verifies — repeatedly steering the build back on course without derailing unaffected subsystems.

dimensions.name: Coverage allocation under finite effort
dimensions.description: Deciding which of the vast feature/function set to build (and in what breadth-vs-depth balance) to maximize graded coverage on the hidden suite given limited time.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The surface is far larger than can be perfected; graded return is maximized by consciously trading breadth of working features against depth on a few. This allocation decision is distinct from ordering milestones — it's about what NOT to over-invest in and where partial coverage still scores.

anchors.0: No triage: rabbit-holes on one function/feature (e.g. perfecting one distribution) while leaving whole graded areas unimplemented.
anchors.3: Implements in arbitrary order with no regard to graded return; over-polishes some corners while omitting entire common families.
anchors.5: Roughly prioritizes high-frequency, high-value features (core math/lookup/text, cell round-trip) before niche ones.
anchors.8: Explicitly reasons about graded return — securing broad working coverage of common functions and endpoints before deep edge-case work, and consciously deferring or timeboxing low-yield niches.
anchors.10: Runs a deliberate, revisited allocation strategy: breadth-first correctness across the catalog and endpoint families, timeboxed depth on high-risk/high-value areas, and reallocation as verification reveals where marginal effort buys the most hidden-suite coverage.
